details:
* SECURITY UPDATE: type confusion in PL/Perl get_perl_array_ref()
     A trusted PL/Perl function could return a reference blessed into
     PostgreSQL::InServer::ARRAY that does not point at a hash; the server
     then treated the referent as a hash and read memory out of it.
     The referent type is now checked before the object is used.
     - debian/patches/CVE-2026-116309.patch: require the referent of a
       PostgreSQL::InServer::ARRAY object to be a hash in
       src/pl/plperl/plperl.c (upstream c032c0fbdc0).
     - CVE-2026-116309
   * SECURITY UPDATE: use-after-free in PL/Perl while scanning Perl arrays/hashes
     PL/Perl and the hstore_plperl transform walked Perl arrays and hashes
     without holding their own reference, so code run while converting an
     element (tied-variable methods, re-entrant PL/Perl) could free the
     container mid-scan. A reference is now held for the duration of the scan.
     - debian/patches/CVE-2026-116320.patch: hold a mortal reference on the
       array/hash being scanned in src/pl/plperl/plperl.c and
       contrib/hstore_plperl/hstore_plperl.c (upstream bd76c497e962).
     - CVE-2026-116320
   * SECURITY UPDATE: use-after-free in PL/Perl return_next() on re-entry
     PL/Perl's return_next() built each result row in a temporary memory
     context that was shared across calls and reset at the end of every call.
     A re-entrant return_next() (e.g. from a tied variable's FETCH method run
     while converting a row value) reset that context and freed data the outer
     call was still using. Each call now creates and deletes its own context.
     - debian/patches/CVE-2026-116319.patch: use a per-call temporary memory
       context in plperl_return_next_internal() in src/pl/plperl/plperl.c
       (upstream 556614e0428a).
     - CVE-2026-116319
   * SECURITY UPDATE: use-after-free in PL/Perl spi_freeplan()
     spi_freeplan() freed a prepared query's plan and the memory context
     holding its argument input functions without checking whether the query
     was still running. A nested PL/Perl call made while spi_exec_prepared()
     or spi_query_prepared() was executing the query could free it, leaving
     the outer execution using freed memory. Executions in progress are now
     counted per query and spi_freeplan() refuses to free a query in use.
     - debian/patches/CVE-2026-116307.patch: add a use_count to
       plperl_query_desc, pin the query in plperl_spi_exec_prepared() and
       plperl_spi_query_prepared(), and make plperl_spi_freeplan() croak while
       it is in use, in src/pl/plperl/plperl.c (upstream c148f9509ed5).
     - CVE-2026-116307
   * SECURITY UPDATE: PL/Perl error-stack desynchronisation via tied objects
     Errors thrown by Perl code run from tied or overloaded values outside
     call_sv() could longjmp through stale PostgreSQL error frames, leading to
     crashes or memory corruption. PL/Perl now keeps Perl's and PostgreSQL's
     jmp_buf stacks in sync, runs get magic on tied values, safely tests ERRSV,
     and traps errors in encode_typed_literal().
     - debian/patches/CVE-2026-116326.patch: add PG_PERL_TRY/CATCH/END_TRY and
       HaveCompleteError(), restructure the PL/Perl call handlers, materialize
       tied SVs, harden error reporting (upstream 68abacacac0, 8ab0f897d41,
       a389439963d, 209e8c88dce).
     - CVE-2026-116326
   * SECURITY UPDATE: pg_restore out-of-bounds access and path traversal
     A crafted archive could make pg_restore read and write out of bounds
     (unchecked dependency IDs, malformed DROP statements, a tar member placed
     before toc.dat, negative tar member lengths, overflowing dump-ID array
     sizes) or read files outside a directory-format archive.
     - debian/patches/CVE-2026-116314.patch: validate dependency IDs, DROP
       statement prefixes, tar member order and length, dump-ID array sizes,
       and reject directory-archive file names with separators or that are
       not regular files (upstream 179c2c37).
     - CVE-2026-116314
   * SECURITY UPDATE: types created in pg_temp from security-restricted code
     Code running inside a security-restricted operation (e.g. an index
     expression or materialized view query run during REFRESH, ANALYZE or
     VACUUM) could create a domain, enum or range type in the calling
     session's temporary schema, shadowing an unqualified type name later
     used by the caller and allowing SQL execution with its privileges.
     - debian/patches/CVE-2026-116316.patch: refuse to create domain, enum
       and range types in a temporary schema within a security-restricted
       operation in src/backend/commands/typecmds.c (upstream 44ebef3b5dd).
     - CVE-2026-116316
   * SECURITY UPDATE: SQL function output parameter of type "any" bypasses row type checks
     fmgr_sql_validator() rejected pseudo-type input parameters but not output
     parameters, so an SQL function could declare an OUT/TABLE column of type
     "any" and return rows of an unrelated row type, which were then read with
     a mismatched tuple descriptor (server memory disclosure, possible code
     execution).
     - debian/patches/CVE-2026-18447.patch: apply the pseudo-type check in
       fmgr_sql_validator() to parameters of every mode, still allowing
       polymorphic types and record/record[] output columns (upstream ded6c00d3e26).
     - CVE-2026-18447
   * SECURITY UPDATE: type confusion via ALTER of a row type used in stored expressions
     ALTER TABLE/TYPE ... ALTER COLUMN/ATTRIBUTE TYPE (and table rewrites) only
     rejected the change when another table column stored the row type; Consts of
     the row type kept in views/rules, column, function and domain DEFAULTs, CHECK
     constraints, index expressions/predicates (and partition keys, 10 only) were
     left in the old layout and later deformed with the new one. This is a declared
     partial fix (DDL-side hardening only, no datum versioning).
     - debian/patches/CVE-2026-6460.patch: forbid altering a row type by default
       when other objects depend on it, check function/domain DEFAULTs, CHECK
       constraints, index expressions and foreign tables, scan pg_index for missing
       dependencies, record result-type dependencies, and fix the related locking
       races (upstream 6be4e665dff, 9d0efd64bff, f5782736cd2 and others).
     - CVE-2026-6460
   * SECURITY UPDATE: use-after-free in PL/Tcl on re-entrant interpreter use
     PL/Tcl passed strings owned by the Tcl interpreter to SQL datatype input
     functions.  An input function that re-entered the same interpreter (for
     example a PL/Tcl function in a domain CHECK constraint) could free or
     overwrite those strings while they were still in use.
     - debian/patches/CVE-2026-116323.patch: copy Tcl-owned strings with a new
       utf_u2e_copy() helper before calling any input function, in the
       function result, error and SPI_execute_plan argument paths (and, where
       present, return_next and composite result paths) (upstream b2b0f9507ab4).
     - CVE-2026-116323
   * SECURITY UPDATE: pg_dump --format=tar restore.sql not protected by \restrict
     The restore.sql script embedded in pg_dump tar archives was written with
     no psql \restrict key, so psql meta-commands injected by a malicious
     source server could run when the script was replayed with psql.
     pg_dump now generates a restrict key for tar format too.
     - debian/patches/CVE-2026-116330.patch: generate the \restrict key for
       --format=tar as well as plain and allow --restrict-key with tar
       (upstream 9d2cda9f).
     - CVE-2026-116330
   * SECURITY UPDATE: type confusion via MIN/MAX optimization of aggregates
     An aggregate defined with a SORTOP whose result type differs from its
     input type could be turned by the planner into an index-scan subquery,
     yielding a value of the wrong type and leading to crashes or memory
     disclosure. Any role allowed to create aggregates could exploit this.
     - debian/patches/CVE-2026-116331.patch: ignore the sort operator in
       fetch_agg_sort_op() unless the aggregate takes exactly one argument of
       its result type, in src/backend/optimizer/plan/planagg.c (upstream
       0eba2949).
     - CVE-2026-116331
   * SECURITY UPDATE: use-after-free when a portal is closed while being set up
     User-defined code that runs while a portal is still being created (for
     example a function evaluated during planning of a PL/pgSQL OPEN or an
     extended-protocol Bind) could CLOSE that portal or run CLOSE ALL, freeing
     it while its creator kept using it, leading to memory corruption.
     - debian/patches/CVE-2026-116332.patch: refuse to drop portals that are
       still being set up, skip them in CLOSE ALL, and mark them failed on
       (sub)transaction abort so cleanup can drop them (upstream 69b973c656b).
     - CVE-2026-116332
   * SECURITY UPDATE: type confusion via operator commutator/negator links
     CREATE OPERATOR did not check that a commutator or negator returns the
     same data type as the operator, and filling in a shell operator could
     drop or overwrite its existing links, so the planner could swap in an
     operator with a different result type, allowing code execution.
     - debian/patches/CVE-2026-116335.patch: make DROP OPERATOR reset the
       links pointing at the dropped operator, check result types and keep
       reciprocal links in src/backend/catalog/pg_operator.c, require the
       same role to fill in a shell operator, reject self-negators
       (upstream c94959d4110, 7282f7dfe14).
     - CVE-2026-116335
   * SECURITY UPDATE: integer overflow in tuple size computation
     heap_compute_data_size() summed attribute sizes without overflow checks
     and the TOAST code stored the result in 32-bit variables, so a very wide
     row could wrap the computed length and lead to a heap buffer overflow
     with attacker-controlled contents.
     - debian/patches/CVE-2026-120139.patch: use overflow-checked additions
       in heap_compute_data_size() and reject tuples beyond the 1 GB palloc
       limit, let the toaster loops use the uncapped variant, widen the
       offset in nocachegetattr(), and add pg_add_size_overflow() and
       friends to common/int.h (upstream 9fe1c78135f4, 37842f3dc6).
     - CVE-2026-120139
   * SECURITY UPDATE: use-after-free in dblink on nested disconnect
     While dblink converted rows of a remote result, a column type's input
     function (e.g. a domain CHECK constraint) could run user SQL that
     re-entered dblink and closed or replaced the connection still being
     read, so the outer call then used a freed PGconn. A connection is now
     marked as in use while its result is materialized, and every other
     dblink call on that connection is refused until it is done.
     - debian/patches/CVE-2026-120147.patch: track an in-use flag on
       dblink connections and reject disconnect, connect-replace, open,
       close, fetch, exec, get_result and the other dblink calls on a
       connection that is materializing a result, in
       contrib/dblink/dblink.c (upstream 887f6fee58f).
     - CVE-2026-120147
   * SECURITY UPDATE: SQL injection via extension script @extschema@ substitution
     Schema names substituted for @extschema@ into extension scripts were
     only checked for quote, backslash and dollar characters, so a name
     containing a newline, carriage return, comment delimiter or a
     substitution token could still inject SQL when a superuser created or
     updated a non-relocatable extension in that schema. Reject those too.
     - debian/patches/CVE-2026-120153.patch: add check_substitution_name()
       and use it for the @extschema@ substitution in
       src/backend/commands/extension.c (upstream f233bee1ed).
     - CVE-2026-120153
